title: Blueberry Yogurt Popsicles
excerpt: Cool off with these creamy homemade popsicles made with Fresh Pick blueberries and Greek yogurt. A colorful dessert that is easy to assemble, with the perfect balance of tartness and sweetness.
imageAlt: Marbled frozen popsicles of fresh blueberries and white yogurt on a rustic tray.

ingredients.text: 1 1/2 cups (375 g) plain unsweetened Greek yogurt

steps: Set aside half a cup of whole Fresh Pick blueberries for the final assembly. The rest of the fruit will provide the vibrant color and concentrated flavor.

In a small pot over low heat, cook the cup and a half of blueberries with half a tablespoon of honey and the teaspoon of lemon juice for 5 minutes, mashing with a fork until you have a light compote. Let it cool to room temperature. We use half the usual sweetener because Fresh Pick blueberries have more natural sugar.
In a bowl, whisk the Greek yogurt with the remaining tablespoon of honey and the vanilla until smooth and silky.
Add the reserved whole fresh blueberries to the yogurt to give every bite crunchy chunks.
In popsicle molds, alternate spoonfuls of the yogurt mixture with the blueberry puree. With the tip of a knife or a toothpick, draw gentle figure-eights or zigzags to create the marbled effect.
Insert the wooden sticks and freeze for at least 6 hours or overnight until completely firm.
To unmold effortlessly, run the base of the molds under warm water for 10 seconds and pull the popsicles out gently by the stick.
tips: Thanks to high-mountain growing in Guasca, these blueberries have a firm, plump skin with their natural bloom intact; when frozen as whole berries inside the yogurt they keep a pleasant texture without becoming watery.
If you don’t have traditional molds, you can use disposable coffee cups or silicone cups; cover them with aluminum foil and push the stick through the center so it stands straight while freezing.
Once unmolded, you can store the popsicles in a zip-top airtight bag, separated by pieces of wax paper, to enjoy whenever you like.
This recipe uses half the usual sweetener: Fresh Pick blueberries have more natural sugar, so we cut it back. Taste it and, if you prefer it sweeter, add a little more.
